places.name: Grand Place (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
places.ai_summary: The Grand Place is the central square of Brussels, known for its ornate guildhalls, the Town Hall, and the Flower Carpet event. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a must-visit landmark.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight or evening illuminations.

places.place_tip: Visit during the Flower Carpet event in August for a spectacular display.

places.name: Atomium
places.ai_summary: The Atomium is a unique architectural landmark in Brussels, representing an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times. It features exhibitions, a panoramic restaurant, and stunning views of the city.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary during special events.

places.place_tip: Take the elevator to the top sphere for panoramic views.

places.name: Manneken Pis
places.ai_summary: Manneken Pis is a famous bronze statue of a little boy urinating into a fountain. It is a beloved symbol of Brussels and has several legends associated with it.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed early in the morning or late in the evening to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Check if the statue is dressed up, as it often wears different costumes.

attribution.description: Manneken Pis in Brussels, Belgium. The original bronze statue was created by Jerome Duquesnoy, 1619. The one exhibited at the junction of Rue de l'Étuve/Stoofstraat and Rue du Chêne/Eikstraat is a replica from 1965.

places.name: Royal Palace of Brussels
places.ai_summary: The Royal Palace of Brussels is the official palace of the King and Queen of the Belgians. It is used for official functions and is open to the public during the summer.

opening_hours.notes: Open to the public from July to September. Check the official website for exact dates.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the Changing of the Guard ceremony, which takes place daily at noon.

places.name: St. Michael and St. Gudula Cathedral
places.ai_summary: The Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula is a Roman Catholic church in Brussels, Belgium. It is the national church of Belgium and a prominent example of Gothic architecture.
places.name_english: St. Michael and St. Gudula Cathedral

opening_hours.notes: Opening hours may vary for religious services and holidays.

places.place_tip: Attend a concert or organ recital for a unique experience.

places.name: Magritte Museum
places.ai_summary: The Magritte Museum is a museum in Brussels dedicated to the works of the Belgian surrealist artist René Magritte. It houses the largest collection of Magritte's paintings in the world.

opening_hours.notes: Last admission one hour before closing.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the nearby Royal Museums of Fine Arts.
places.address: Rue de la Régence 3, 1000 Brussels, Belgium

places.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
places.ai_summary: The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium is an institution that groups together several art museums in Brussels, including the Old Masters Museum and the Modern Museum.

opening_hours.notes: Check the official website for temporary exhibitions and events.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the Magritte collection and the modern art section.
places.address: Rue de la Régence 3, 1000 Brussels, Belgium

places.name: Mini-Europe
places.ai_summary: Mini-Europe is a miniature park located in Brussels, where you can see replicas of famous European landmarks and buildings. It's a great place for families and tourists of all ages.

opening_hours.notes: Last admission one hour before closing.

places.place_tip: Visit the park in the afternoon for the best lighting for photos.

places.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
places.ai_summary: Parc du Cinquantenaire is a public park in the European Quarter of Brussels. It features impressive arches, museums, and beautiful gardens.

opening_hours.notes: Gates close at 20:00, but the park is accessible on foot at all times.

places.place_tip: Explore the museums within the park, such as the AutoWorld and the Royal Museum of the Armed Forces.

places.name: Mont des Arts
places.ai_summary: Mont des Arts is a historic site in Brussels, known for its beautiful gardens, fountains, and panoramic views of the city. It's a popular spot for tourists and locals alike.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during the day for the views and gardens.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby Royal Library of Belgium and the Brussels Park.

places.name: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
places.ai_summary: The Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert is a glazed shopping arcade in Brussels, Belgium. It is one of the oldest shopping arcades in Europe and is known for its luxury shops, cafes, and beautiful architecture.

opening_hours.notes: Some shops may have extended hours, especially during the holiday season.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a coffee or chocolate at one of the famous cafes inside the galleries.

places.name: European Parliament & EU Quarter
places.ai_summary: The European Parliament is the directly elected parliamentary institution of the European Union. The EU Quarter in Brussels is home to several important EU buildings and institutions.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours are available but must be booked in advance.

places.place_tip: Visit the Parc Leopold and the Berlaymont building while in the area.

places.name: Place du Grand Sablon
places.ai_summary: Place du Grand Sablon is a square in the Brussels-Capital Region, known for its antique shops, chocolatiers, and the beautiful Church of Our Blessed Lady of the Sablon.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning for the antique market (weekends only).

places.place_tip: Try the hot chocolate at one of the famous chocolatiers in the square.
places.address: Place du Grand Sablon, 1000 Brussels, Belgium

places.name: Comic Strip Center
places.ai_summary: The Comic Strip Center is a museum in Brussels dedicated to the art of comic strips. It features exhibitions on the history of comics, original artwork, and a comic book shop.

opening_hours.notes: Last admission one hour before closing.

places.place_tip: Don't forget to visit the gift shop for unique comic-related souvenirs.

places.name: Bozar Art Centre
places.ai_summary: Bozar is a multidisciplinary cultural complex in Brussels, hosting a wide range of events including concerts, exhibitions, and film screenings. It is located in the Palace of the Academies.

opening_hours.notes: Check the official website for the event schedule and ticket prices.

places.place_tip: Explore the nearby Mont des Arts and the Royal Palace.

places.name: Train World Museum
places.ai_summary: Train World is a railway museum in Brussels, showcasing the history of trains and rail transport in Belgium. The museum features interactive exhibits and a large collection of locomotives and carriages.

opening_hours.notes: Last admission one hour before closing.

places.place_tip: Take the time to explore the interactive exhibits, especially if traveling with children.

places.name: Parc de Bruxelles
places.ai_summary: Parc de Bruxelles, also known as Brussels Park, is the largest urban park in the city center of Brussels. It is a popular place for locals and tourists to relax, walk, and enjoy nature.

opening_hours.notes: Gates close at 20:00, but the park is accessible on foot at all times.

places.place_tip: Visit the Royal Palace and the Magritte Museum, located at the park's edge.

places.name: Delirium Café
places.ai_summary: Delirium Café is a famous bar in Brussels, known for its extensive beer selection and vibrant atmosphere. It holds the Guinness World Record for the most beers available commercially.

opening_hours.notes: Happy hour from 17:00 to 19:00. Check the website for special events.

places.place_tip: Try the local Belgian beers and enjoy the lively atmosphere.
places.address: Impasse de la Fidélité 4, 1000 Brussels, Belgium

places.name: Saint Catherine’s Square
places.ai_summary: Saint Catherine’s Square is a picturesque square in Brussels, known for its beautiful church, vibrant atmosphere, and proximity to the seafood restaurants of Rue Sainte-Catherine.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the evening for the lively atmosphere.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a meal at one of the seafood restaurants nearby.

places.name: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken
places.ai_summary: The Royal Greenhouses of Laeken are part of the Royal Castle of Laeken, the official residence of the King and Queen of the Belgians. The greenhouses are open to the public during the spring and showcase a vast collection of plants and flowers.

opening_hours.notes: Open to the public from April to October. Check the official website for exact dates.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with a tour of the Royal Castle of Laeken.
places.address: Avenue du Parc Royal 1, 1020 Brussels, Belgium
